title: Speed and Motion
seo_title: Year 9 Science: Speed and Motion Worksheets (Speed = Distance ÷ Time, Graphs)
standard_text: Speed and the quantitative relationship between average speed, distance and time (speed = distance ÷ time); the representation of a journey on a distance-time graph; relative motion: trains and cars passing one another; forces being needed to cause objects to stop or start moving, or to change their speed or direction of motion (qualitative only); change depending on direction of force and its size.
meta_desc: Free Year 9 science worksheets on speed and motion: speed, distance and time calculations, m/s and km/h, distance-time graphs, relative motion and balanced and unbalanced forces. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: On a distance-time graph, steeper means faster and flat means stopped.
body_html:
How to think about it

Speed tells you how far something goes in each second (or hour).

  • speed = distance ÷ time; distance = speed × time; time = distance ÷ speed.
  • On a distance-time graph, a steeper line means faster; a flat line means stopped.
  • Balanced forces keep the motion the same; an unbalanced (resultant) force changes speed or direction.
Example

300 m in 60 s?

300 ÷ 60

Answer: 5 m/s

Example

72 km/h in m/s?

72 × 1,000 ÷ 3,600

Answer: 20 m/s

Common mistakes

  • Writing speed = time ÷ distance.
  • Thinking a flat line means a steady speed.
  • Thinking a moving object needs an unbalanced force.

faq.a: Divide the distance travelled by the time taken: speed = distance ÷ time. Use m/s for metres and seconds, km/h for kilometres and hours.

faq.q: How do you read a distance-time graph?
faq.a: A straight sloping line means a steady speed; steeper is faster. A flat line means the object has stopped.
Speed compared with another moving object. Two cars at the same speed side by side are not moving relative to each other.
